correctness.rationale: The realignment index convention gives exact left/right identity-vector partial-trace identities. Zero centered marginals force those identity vectors into the left and right kernels, while the maximally mixed product marginal term is exactly a rank-one scalar block of singular value 1/sqrt(d_A d_B). This proves r_k(rho)=r_k(tilde rho)+c^(2k). Scaling any feasible centered moment vector by sqrt(G) and appending c matches every requested uncentered moment, and Cauchy--Schwarz proves sqrt(G)+c<=1. Boundary assumptions d_A,d_B>=2 ensure G>0. The proof does not rely on finite experiments.

Targeted semantic record and web searches returned no equivalent statement.

value.rationale: The theorem answers an explicit open question from a current paper on a broad and standard state class (all finite-dimensional locally maximally mixed bipartite states) and does so simultaneously for every finite number of accessible moments. The quantitative alpha_m transfer inequality is reusable and explains structurally why moment-level dominance holds in this class; it is not a parameter substitution or a recomputation of a known table.
